title: shrinkwrap
body:
## shrinkwrap

Moves each vertex of a copy of the input mesh onto the surface of a second mesh, the target, using Blender's Shrinkwrap modifier with its default Nearest Surface Point method; mode decides how vertices may sit relative to the target and offset keeps a gap. Use it to drape a patch, label or coating onto another shape. The target is not changed and is rendered only if it is listed as visible.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The input needs enough vertices to follow curvature; subdivide a plane before wrapping.
- Both meshes must be graph nodes; the target is resolved through its own transform in world space.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `shrinkwrap`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `data` |
| `target` | one node | yes | `data` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `offset` | Distance to keep from the target surface after projection; positive values float the wrapped mesh off the target to avoid z-fighting or to model a coating thickness. | `{"type":"number"}` | `0` |
| `mode` | How each projected vertex may sit relative to the target (Blender wrap_mode). ON_SURFACE snaps every vertex onto the surface, offset towards its original side. OUTSIDE and INSIDE only move vertices that are on the wrong side, leaving others where they are, for keeping a shell outside or inside a body. ABOVE_SURFACE snaps to the surface and applies offset exactly along the target normal, for an even coating. | `{"type":"enum","values":["ON_SURFACE","OUTSIDE","INSIDE","ABOVE_SURFACE"]}` | `"ON_SURFACE"` |
